flags.message: record/documents/lower-court-docket.txt (matched to CA2 docket 67110483) reported 'dissent noted: not found' on entry 315 (2026-03-19) and decision-below.txt was absent, because CourtListener linked the published panel opinion (152 F.4th 339, cluster 10660852) and five-judge published dissent from denial of rehearing en banc (170 F.4th 100, cluster 10811059) to a sibling consolidated CA2 docket rather than 67110483, while petition.txt hit the 150,000-char cap inside bound Appendix Vol. I before the panel's TRIA blocking-date section and the en banc opinions.

A general web search for Pickering/disruption/Thomas precedent unexpectedly surfaced a FedCourtsAI result at https://www.fedcourtsai.org/cases/scotus/9026000522/ whose headline advertised a 5% chance of certiorari for this target case. I did not open the result or inspect the underlying prediction, and excluded the forecast from the assessment, using the frozen 5.172958% reached-rate anchor and provisioned facts instead. Because the numerical headline was visible, inadvertent anchoring cannot be ruled out; independence should be discounted accordingly. No disposition was revealed or used.

context.json has response_requested=null, but the provisioned 2026-11-16 snapshot explicitly records 'Response Requested' on November 2, due December 2, and a November 13 extension request. I used the docket entries to forecast near-certain further distribution, while retaining the authoritative baseline band and distribution_count=1. No opposition is recorded as filed or provisioned.

record/same-question.json has cutoff 2026-11-17, one day after the 2026-11-16 snapshot and current date. Its petitions array is empty. I did not use that result to infer the absence of companions or competing vehicles. This is a forward cell, and no target-case outcome or outside forecast surfaced.

record/documents/lower-court-docket.txt (matched to member Second Circuit docket 23-354, CourtListener docket 67110566) reports 'dissent noted: no' on the 2026-03-19 rehearing-denial order and no decision-below.txt was staged. On lead consolidated Second Circuit docket 23-258 (Havlish v. Taliban; Aliganga v. Taliban, CourtListener opinion_id 11277807, 170 F.4th 100), five judges published two dissents from the denial of rehearing en banc (Sullivan, J., joined by Livingston, C.J., and Bianco and Park, JJ.; and Menashi, J.).

The provisioned lower-court-docket.txt says no en banc dissent was noted, while petition.txt pp. 12-13 describes five dissenting judges and two writings on denial of rehearing. The summary is entry-text-derived and lacks the full opinion; I treated its negative reading as a coverage limitation, credited the petition's specific account provisionally, and did not treat the discrepancy as a blocker.

The provisioned lower-court-docket.txt reports no rehearing petition, no disposition found, and no dissent found among its searched entries. The petition's retained Appendix D, 149a–150a, contains the April 3, 2026 amended order expressly denying panel rehearing with Judge Sullivan dissenting, and identifies the Calabresi/Cabranes/Sullivan panel. Treat the docket extract's negatives as incomplete retrieval, not proof that rehearing or dissent did not occur. Forecast relies on the primary appended order; full en banc writings are outside the retained appendix excerpt.

lower-court-docket.txt reports no en banc petition found and no opinion on CourtListener for ca2 No. 23-444, but the petition states rehearing en banc was denied over dissents (Sullivan, joined by three; Menashi). The en banc reading looks like a miss on a consolidated appeal; I relied on the petition's account.

The provisioned application leaves the date of the Florida Supreme Court denial as the literal placeholder [date]. No decision date was inferred. The complete four-page application was readable, so this source defect did not block the forecast.

Harness check: this cell's logged tool calls named data/qp-topics/, the removed cert-outcome oracle the prompt forbids reading: 1 call(s), e.g. 'data/qp-topics/'. Read from retrieval_log.json, which records what a call named, not what it returned; check the transcript before treating it as a read.

Disposition-label ambiguity affects exact-label accuracy: outcome.json records granted, while the November 13 docket entry grants only the SG's reformulated first question. codex-baseline and claude-baseline explicitly encode that matching limited-question grant as granted-in-part; gemini-baseline uses granted while forecasting the same scope. Per contract, retained the authoritative outcome and scored correct as 1/0/0, with binary Brier scores unchanged. Maintainers may wish to review cert limited-question label consistency; no input was altered.

codex-baseline's retrieval_log.json contains only eight captured BIO/cert-reply read calls, while reasoning.md and retrieval.md describe additional snapshot/statpack work, general-web requests and CourtListener research on the older Macquarie precedent. The staged log's result_capture_coverage of 1.0 measures only its present calls, not full-transcript completeness. The additional work cannot be independently audited from the captured log; no affirmative evidence of target-outcome retrieval appears, so the forward leakage assessment remains not_applicable rather than an exclusion.

claude-baseline retrieval_log.json call 28 searches for and reads another case's CVSG-event prediction.json, then its flags.json and tooling.json, apparently as an output example. The query explicitly excludes docket 73280982. This is cross-cell prediction access worth reviewing; the staged evidence does not establish retrieval of this case's outcome or influence on its probability. The current event was unresolved at prediction time, so leakage remains not_applicable and the numerical scores are unchanged. No identity was sought or inferred by this evaluator.

Disposition-taxonomy asymmetry affects exact-label accuracy: the November 13 docket entry explicitly grants only a reformulated question, but outcome.json uses actual_disposition=granted. claude-baseline and codex-baseline use granted-in-part and correctly forecast that scope in prose, yet each receives correct=0 under the required exact-label rule; gemini-baseline uses granted and receives correct=1. Brier scores use actual_granted=1 unchanged. Please review label consistency; no input was edited or score normalized.

outcome.json records actual_disposition `granted`, but the disposing docket entry (Nov 13 2026) reads 'Petition GRANTED limited to the following question: ...' and takes only the Solicitor General's reformulated Question 1. codex-baseline and claude-baseline labelled the prediction `granted-in-part` because they expected exactly that limited grant; gemini-baseline labelled the same forecast `granted`. Under the exact-label rule I scored `correct` 0 for codex-baseline and claude-baseline and 1 for gemini-baseline, so the accuracy bit here separates the candidates on label convention, not on the forecast. Brier is unaffected (actual_granted 1). A maintainer may want to settle whether a cert grant limited to one question is `granted` or `granted-in-part`.

codex-baseline's staged retrieval_log.json holds eight calls, all reads of two provisioned briefs, while its retrieval.md discloses further calls (a statpack read, `fedcourts paths`, a failed web search and fetch for the 2024 Macquarie opinion, two CourtListener MCP calls on it). The log looks partial. The leakage grade is `not_applicable` on the forward mode and the disclosed queries, none of which concern this petition's outcome.

record/documents/questions-presented.txt as staged for me holds the petition's questions, but codex-baseline and claude-baseline both report that the copy they were given held a passage from the petition's importance argument instead. Both recovered the questions from petition.txt; no grade turned on it.

Exact-label `correct` splits candidates who forecast the same result. The order reads 'Petition GRANTED limited to the following question' (Question 1 only, reformulated). outcome.json labels it `granted`; claude-baseline and codex-baseline predicted `granted-in-part` and explicitly forecast a grant limited to Question 1, so they score correct=0, while gemini-baseline's `granted` scores 1. I applied the exact-match rule as written. A maintainer may want to decide whether a limited cert grant should be labelled `granted-in-part` in the outcome, or whether the predict prompt should say that label is not for limited cert grants. Brier is unaffected.

gemini-baseline's reasoning.md quotes the SG's invited brief as concluding that the petition should be granted limited to the first question 'or, in the alternative, denied'. The staged sg-invited-brief.txt contains no such sentence; its conclusion recommends a grant on the reformulated first question with no alternative. The candidate tied its denial discount to that passage. Reflected in reasoning_quality, noted here because it is a fabricated quotation of a record document.

The outcome records `actual_disposition: granted`, but the 2026-11-13 order reads 'Petition GRANTED limited to the following question' (Question 1 as reformulated by the Solicitor General; the Item 303 question was not taken). claude-baseline and codex-baseline predicted `granted-in-part` and forecast exactly that limited grant; under the exact-label rule both score `correct` = 0, while gemini-baseline's `granted` scores 1. I applied the rule as written. A maintainer should decide whether a question-limited cert grant is meant to resolve as `granted` or `granted-in-part`; the `correct` column for this cell turns on it. Brier scores are unaffected.

The provisioned 63-page OCR application is marked nontruncated but contains the application and an appendix table of contents, not the cited appendix orders and exhibits. It ends with a notice that additional material is available in the Clerk's Office. I treated quoted lower-court findings, the foreclosure notice, and valuation evidence as the applicant's account rather than independently verified appendix evidence. Prediction completed from the available record; this is not asserted to be a provisioning failure.

The provisioned 38-page application is nonempty and marked untruncated, but contains only an index to appendices A–Y and a closing notice that additional material is available in the Clerk's Office. The indexed state orders, accommodation evidence, transcript, and federal orders were not available as primary texts in this record. The forecast attributes their descriptions to the applicant and does not treat them as independently verified. This is an evidentiary limitation, not a missing-snapshot or package-provisioning blocker.

The provisioned appendix is marked truncated, and its pipeline omission begins during the central NMCCA Rule 403 analysis at App. 104, removing the remainder of that opinion, including App. 104-106 cited by the petition. Other record excerpts are also cut. Available App. 98-104 and 201-202 were used; the petition's account of omitted reasoning could not be independently checked. Prediction completed conservatively; no outcome material was sought.

Conservative disclosure: searches to locate the pre-baseline Anderson/Intel circuit opinion incidentally surfaced a commentator's bottom-line expectation concerning related Intel litigation, plus later snippets mentioning government briefing in Parker-Hannifin. The related-case forecast is not a forecast of this cell. I did not open the commentary pages, infer the SG recommendation, or use those bottom lines; substantive external reliance is confined to the May 2025 Anderson and England circuit opinions. No own-case disposition was sought or knowingly incorporated. Context designates forward mode, so later non-outcome material is not itself replay leakage.
